appearance_facts.fact: The pie chart is titled 'Global Energy Consumption by Source'.
The chart is divided into four colored segments.
The largest segment is orange-red, labeled 'Nuclear (45%)'.
The second largest segment is red, labeled 'Hydroelectric (30%)'.
The third largest segment is yellow, labeled 'Fossil Fuels (15%)'.
The smallest segment is light orange, labeled 'Renewables (10%)'.
The segments are arranged clockwise from top-right: Nuclear, Hydroelectric, Fossil Fuels, Renewables.
Each segment's percentage is printed in white text within its area.

printed_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Global Energy Consumption by Source'.
The Fossil Fuels segment is labeled 'Fossil Fuels (15%)'.
The chart uses color to distinguish segments: Nuclear (orange-red), Hydroelectric (red), Fossil Fuels (yellow), Renewables (light orange).
The percentage values are printed in white text within each segment.
The segments are visually proportional to their labeled percentages.

public_definitions: The goal is to identify the largest global energy consumption source category from the dashboard and route that source record to priority source monitoring.
The comparison scope is the global energy mix dashboard, specifically the pie chart titled 'Global Energy Consumption by Source'.
The rules are to select the category with the highest percentage share from the chart and route it to priority monitoring.
